subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers adopt or rebase the open conflicting fork PR, replace it with a fresh same-repo fix, or close that fork path before queueing another fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug shape is clear, but an open fork PR still uses closing syntax and is conflicting, so automation should not create a competing fix until maintainers choose the branch path.

options.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
options.body: Close or supersede the stale fork branch and land a focused same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async displayName hydration.

options.title: Adopt Or Rebase Fork PR
options.body: Have a maintainer or contributor update the fork PR to current main, add missing coverage and proof, then review it as the landing candidate.

options.title: Keep Waiting On Fork PR
options.body: Leave this issue blocked on the existing fork PR even though it is conflicting and has not updated since April 2026.

recommendation.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the stale fork branch and land a focused same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async displayName hydration.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is the committer on the original title-picker commits and is the strongest available routing signal for deciding the branch path.
